collection.description: A villager wakes up feeling absolutely marvellous.

ask.text:
(Name) wakes up feeling absolutely marvellous. The sun is warm on (his/her) mat, the smell of roasting breadfruit is drifting in through the doorway, and (he/she) slept like a stone. (He/She) stretches, gets up, and runs through the day in (his/her) head. (He/She) knows how to farm, how to build, how to cook, how to climb. (He/She) knows the names of everyone in the village, and their children's names, and their goats' names.
Except one. (His/her) own.
It's gone. Clean out of (his/her) head, like a dream on waking. (He/She) stands there in the doorway, opening and closing (his/her) mouth, and nothing comes.
Then (he/she) notices the pale flowers. In the night a moon-vine has crept in over the doorway, the one the elders call forget-me-all, and its sweet smell is still thick in the hut and drifting out over the village. Should (name) ask around until someone remembers, or just make up a new name?

c1o1.text: The trouble is that, the moment (he/she) asks, everyone else realises they've forgotten it too. And nobody wants to admit it. So each of them, very confidently, tells (him/her) a different name. The baker says one thing. The fisher says another. (His/her) own mother says something that turns out to be the name of a cousin. By lunchtime (name) has been given nine names and none of them feels right, because the moon-vine took the real one, and without it (name) is left with no name at all: just "?". The real one never comes back.

c1o2.text: Nobody can quite remember. They scratch their heads, they look at each other, they say "it's on the tip of my tongue." Then a very small child tugs at (name)'s wrap, looks up at (him/her), and says (his/her) name, without the slightest hesitation, as if it were the most obvious thing in the world. It all comes rushing back at once. (Name) is so grateful that (he/she) picks the child up, spins (him/her) round, and gives (him/her) (his/her) dessert that night, and the next night too.

c1.text: (Name) wanders out into the village and starts asking people, as casually as (he/she) can manage: "Morning! Remind me, what's my name again?" People look at (him/her) very oddly...

c2o1.text: ...(renamed)! It's a fine name. It rolls off the tongue. It sounds as if it's always been (his/hers). Everyone tries it out, and it fits so well that within a week nobody remembers the old one at all, and within a month even (his/her) mother uses it without thinking. Every so often, (name) gets a funny feeling that (he/she) used to be called something else. But (he/she) can never remember what.

c2o2.text: ...well. (He/She) stands there. (He/She) can't think of one. Not a single name comes into (his/her) head, good or bad. So (he/she) shrugs. And every time someone asks after that, (he/she) shrugs again. Whatever the moon-vine took, it isn't giving back, and (he/she) is left with no name at all: just "?". To everyone's surprise, (name) rather likes it. "It's honest," (he/she) says. "Nobody really knows who they are anyway."

c2.text: (Name) decides that if (his/her) name can't be bothered to stay, (he/she) can't be bothered to go looking for it. (He/She) stands in the middle of the village, clears (his/her) throat, and announces that from now on (he/she) shall be called...
